spec.title: Triangle multiplication, line by line (AF3 SI Algorithms 12 and 13)
spec.caption: N tokens, 128 channels. Outgoing combines the edges leaving i and j, incoming the edges arriving at them. Every weight matrix W acts on one pair vector at a time; only the sum over k mixes different pairs.
spec.main_latex: z_{ij} \leftarrow z_{ij} + g_{ij} \odot W_o\,\mathrm{LN}\Big(\sum_{k=1}^{N} a_{ik} \odot b_{jk}\Big)

steps.explanation: Normalise every pair vector on its own.

steps.latex: a_{ij} = \sigma(W_1 \bar z_{ij}) \odot W_2 \bar z_{ij}, \qquad b_{ij} = \sigma(W_3 \bar z_{ij}) \odot W_4 \bar z_{ij}
steps.explanation: Two gated projections of each pair, 128 channels each. a_ik is what the edge i→k contributes, b_jk what the edge j→k contributes; the sigmoid gates let the network silence edges it does not trust.
Channel by channel this is an ordinary N × N matrix product. Entry (i, j) is the dot product of row i of A and row j of B: large when i and j say similar things about the same third tokens k.

steps.latex: g_{ij} = \sigma(W_g \bar z_{ij}), \qquad z_{ij} \leftarrow z_{ij} + g_{ij} \odot W_o\,\mathrm{LN}(\cdot)
steps.explanation: Normalise the summed message, project it back, gate it with the pair's own gate and add it to the pair as a residual update.
The second variant uses columns instead of rows: the edges k→i and k→j that arrive at i and j from a common k. It is the outgoing update applied to the transposed pair tensor.

steps.latex: \text{cost: } N^2 \text{ pairs} \times N \text{ third tokens} \times 128 \text{ channels} = \mathcal O(N^3)
steps.explanation: Every pair looks at every third token, which is why the Pairformer, not the denoiser, dominates the cost of large complexes.

The intuition. Replace (sum, product) by (min, sum) and the same pattern becomes the triangle inequality: two short edges through k force the third edge to be short. The network learns its own soft version of this rule, in 128 channels and with learned gates.
